entries.note: Cook 2001 (PMID 11549370, OA) resolves; quote verbatim in abstract. Opening untested at first 22E9 use is right. Serum biomarkers in Genovese 2020 are another compartment than joint washout; see rule question 6.
Achuthan 2016 (PMID 27525438, epub 2016-08-15) resolves; quote verbatim. Separate track justified: GSK's Phase 2a was built around the GM-CSF-CCL17 axis (paper title), so the class relied on it.

Genovese 2020 (PMID 38279363) resolves; quote verbatim in abstract. Registry NCT02799472 (2018-11-16) reports CCL17 vs placebo ratio 0.56 wk8 p=0.017, 0.52 wk12 p=0.026, so 2018 and same hold; downstream tier right.
Cook 2001 resolves; quote verbatim. Opening untested; no human exposure target in any 22E9 paper (Koch 2012 abstract confirms a mouse-only PK/PD model, pre-clinic, not post-hoc).

Quote verbatim in abstract; model_src Koch 2012 resolves. Target not sustained on every-other-week maintenance is decision 4 case 1 (never reached) more than case 4; dose contra holds either way, but case 1 makes BAROQUE efficacy untested (efficacy 3).
Cook 2001 resolves; quote verbatim. Opening entry. NCT00995449 (9 patients, 'Program refocus', results 2012-09-25) and NCT01023256 (2014-05-08) dates verified; correctly no-status facts.

Taylor 2019 (PMID 30999929, OA) resolves; quote verbatim; registry NCT02379091 (2018-09-14) primary -0.92 p=0.010 at 150 mg. Full text cites 22E9 as a bare citation, so comparison_stated false is right.

entries.rule: decision 4 (#32: missed primary + significant secondary is untested unless the source calls it a match; and case 1 of the dose tie)
entries.note: Quote verbatim. Missed primary plus significant secondaries (registry, 90 mg: DAS28-CRP change p=0.022, EULAR p=0.033, CDAI p=0.032, pain p=0.039) is untested unless the source calls it a match; Buckley calls it neither. Dose case 1 agrees. Fold into patient_trials.
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 4 #32: DAS28-CRP remission primary missed at all five doses, secondaries significant at 90 mg, Buckley's interpretation calls it neither match nor miss; the rule has no dose-count carve-out. Untested; efficacy 4 becomes the track's first contra, drop strengthens.

entries.rule: decision 7 (dating: earliest admissible source) with decision 2 (tier 5 patient-side)
entries.note: Taylor 2023 (PMID 37696589, OA) resolves; quote verbatim; contra holds (primary and all secondaries missed, not an active-comparator ranking miss). GSK release 2022-10-27 made the miss public first. If efficacy 3 is corrected this is the status change: drop strengthens.
Dranoff 1994 (PMID 8171324) resolves; quote verbatim in abstract. Own track for the germline null and opening untested are right.
Cook 2001 resolves; quote verbatim. Silence with no patient harm to test it stays untested; the entry changes nothing and is harmless.

entries.rule: decision 5 (dated to the first patient dataset that could have shown the harm) with decision 7
entries.note: Quote verbatim; contra/opposite follows decision 5. Behrens 2015 (epub 2014-02-17, PMC4431325) states 'Surfactant D levels remained normal and there was no overall pattern of PFT alterations in MOR103-treated subjects'; NEXUS 2019 full text reports no KL-6/SP-D trend. Earliest dataset 2014, fallback 2018.

Weinblatt 2025 (PMID 40044198, OA) resolves; quote verbatim; NCT04333147 results 2024-02-07, 2915 exposed, terminated for the programme decision. Strengthens is right; registry AE tables could date it 2024 but carry no quotable sentence.

Kitamura 1999 (PMID 10499925) resolves; quote verbatim in abstract. Own track and opening untested right; Uchida 2004/2009 threshold predates every trial, so not retro. human_genetic is the nearest enum for an acquired state (rule question 5).

Behrens 2015 full text: quote verbatim; SP-D measured 'because high levels of GM-CSF autoantibodies have been associated with' PAP, so comparison_stated holds. Same accepted on #51/#58: null predicted below threshold, CCL17 only halved (engagement 3). Hinge stays rule question 5.

Taylor 2019 PMC6471864: quote verbatim; lungs monitored 'because of the theoretical risk of developing PAP' citing Inoue 2008 autoimmune cohort. Registry NCT02379091 results 2018-09-14 verified; strengthens, still sub-threshold.

Weinblatt 2025 (PMID 40044198): quote verbatim in abstract; NCT04333147 results 2024-02-07 verified, registry AE tables carry no PAP sentence (as safety 4). Same strengthens holds on the same conditional reading; turns contra only if neutralisation shown complete.

Protocol PDF (NCT04134728, approved 2020-01-21, uploaded 2023-01-31) pp. 20-21: quote verbatim, split by the page break after '26-week IV'. Untested keeps the held ceiling counted once in dose (decision 16); #58 could read it same (new rule question).

Protocol p. 36: margin sentence verbatim, intact. 26-week GLP study predates BAROQUE, so first use precedes 2020 but is unsourced; 2020 is the approval date, as an EPAR carries its opinion year. Registry-hosted protocol as tier 3: new rule question.

Taylor 2023 (PMID 37696589): quote verbatim in abstract, general AE sentence rather than lung-specific; registry results 2023-07-17 verified. Decision 16 same: NOEL margin stated for 150 mg weekly before contRAst, patients dosed to it, no toxicity; not retro.

Weinblatt 2025: PAP-specific sentence verbatim in abstract; 2915 patients up to 896 days at the covered dose. Strengthens the held ceiling; harm counted once, in dose, per decision 16. Year 2025 as on safety 4/8.

missing: Human anti-GM-CSF-autoantibody PAP as the human loss-of-function analogue the trials themselves relied on for lung monitoring (Behrens 2015 PMC4431325: 'Because high levels of GM-CSF autoantibodies have been associated with idiopathic pulmonary alveolar proteinosis ... serum surfactant D levels were measured'; Kitamura 1999 doi:10.1084/jem.190.6.875; Uchida 2004 doi:10.1182/blood-2003-05-1565). A separate track: it predicts PAP only above a neutralising-autoantibody threshold, so no PAP at partial pharmacological neutralisation may be same for it while contra for the knockout.

MOR103 Phase 1b/2a (Behrens 2015, doi:10.1136/annrheumdis-2013-204816, PMID 24534756, epub 2014-02-17, NCT01023256 results 2014-05-08, n=96) and NEXUS (Taylor 2019 full text, PMC6471864: 'biomarkers with the potential for early detection of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (carcinoembryonic antigen, KL-6, and SP-D), there were no trends associated with namilumab treatment') as earlier patient datasets on the knockout PAP track; the draft said the abstracts lacked a quotable sentence but the OA full texts have one.

GSK press release 2022-10-27 'GSK provides update on contRAst phase III programme for otilimab' (gsk.com; tier 5): contRAst 3 'did not demonstrate statistical significance on the primary endpoint of ACR20', contRAst 1 and 2 met theirs, 'GSK has decided not to progress with regulatory submissions'. The draft's note says 'dropped in 2022' but no entry cites it; it is the earliest public record of the miss.

Importable safety datasets for members with no RA safety data in the draft: lenzilumab LIVE-AIR COVID-19 Phase 3 (Temesgen 2022, doi:10.1016/S2213-2600(21)00494-X, PMID 34863332) and namilumab CATALYST (Fisher 2022, doi:10.1016/S2213-2600(21)00460-4, PMID 34922649), transferable with imported_from per decision 12; strengthens-only, no status change.
rule_questions: Decision 4 #32 vs the primary-endpoint rule: BAROQUE missed DAS28-CRP remission at all five doses (best p=0.053) but had significant secondaries (DAS28-CRP change, EULAR response, SDAI/CDAI, pain at 90 mg) and the source's conclusion calls it neither match nor miss. Does 'missed primary + significant secondary is untested' cover a dose-ranging trial that missed at every dose, or only a single-dose miss? This is the hinge for efficacy 3.

Decision 4 case 4 ('reached, failed, a higher dose later worked: efficacy contra then same') vs decision 6 (contra sticky unless patient_signal_reversed) and lint: when the corrected weekly regimen then met ACR20 in contRAst 1 and 2, can efficacy return to same without patient_signal_reversed? The draft could not apply case 4 as written; under the proposed correction (BAROQUE untested) the conflict disappears, but the rule text still contradicts itself.

Dating by tier 5: decision 7 names 'the earliest admissible source that makes the comparison', and a sponsor press release (GSK 2022-10-27) preceded the registry (2023-07-17) and paper (2023-09-11) records of the contRAst 3 miss by a year. Does the press release set year, and if so should the entry carry the tier-5 src with trial_unreported, or keep the tier-1 src with the earlier year?

Decision 5 'first patient dataset that could have shown the harm': for a slowly developing harm such as PAP, what exposure qualifies: a 4-week IV course with SP-D and PFT monitoring (MOR103, 2014), 12 weeks with KL-6/SP-D (NEXUS, 2018 registry), or about a year (BAROQUE, 2020)? The proposed 2014 date rests on the trial having monitored the harm's own surrogate.

model_kind for an acquired human loss-of-function state: anti-GM-CSF-autoantibody PAP is the closest human analogue of the class's pharmacology but is autoimmune, not genetic; human_genetic is the nearest enum. Should it be its own track, and does a model that predicts harm only above a neutralisation threshold score same when partial pharmacological neutralisation produced no harm?

Engagement readout compartment: the 22E9 model's PD readout was joint-washout TNF and IL-1beta; patients were sampled only in serum (Genovese 2020: no change in 110 of 112 serum biomarkers). Is a serum measurement of the same analyte admissible (contra on the 22E9 engagement track) or inadmissible (untested, as drafted)?

Model-side admissibility of a registry-hosted trial protocol: decision 2 tier 3 is 'registry results record with posted outcome data' and #125 makes a registry protocol narrative with no results a sponsor statement; the contRAst 3 protocol (IND 121958, IRB-approved 2020-01-21, uploaded 2023-01-31 to a record with results) is the only public carrier of otilimab's unpublished GLP monkey NOEL. Is it tier 3 on the model side, or a sponsor statement like tier 5 ('never for the model side'), which would delete the cyno-tox-otilimab-26wk track? If admitted, does its year follow approval (2020) or upload (2023)?

A toxic ceiling that held: decision 16 scores the stated NOEL margin in dose (same) and counts a window-closing harm once, but says nothing about a correctly placed margin with no harm. #58 (null-null is same when the model made the null a prediction) would also score the cyno safety cell same, flipping the safety headline from the knockout's contra; the draft leaves it untested. Is a held ceiling counted once (dose only) like a closing harm?
